# SPE Round 3 Plan

Round 3 fixes the outage lookup in C (F4) and the retry cost in D (F6). It also adds 10 harder tickets and raises trials to 5 per cell. I start every number from round 2's measured value. I move a number only when this round changes something that should move it. Round 2 needs this rule because the naive guess beat 4 of my 5 predictions.

Defaults I chose because the situation did not give them:
- I assume the original ticket set is 20 tickets (T01 to T20). I will confirm the real count at the specify step and use it.
- I predict only the cells that have a round 2 baseline, plus the new cells named below. The workflow still measures the other cells, but they are not scored as predictions.

## 1. Specify

**Transcript.** I will save your prompt verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`.

**Decisions on the round 2 proposals**

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 is the cause of C's priority miss. Splitting the status check back out is C's one change this round. |
| P2 | Adopt, as a separate slice | A and B are at 0.86 on the original set. That leaves little room to tell the configs apart. I report the hard tickets as their own slice, so the original 20 stay comparable with round 2. |
| P3 | Reject as written. D gets a retry cap instead (default) | F6 has a clear fix. Dropping D would leave F6 untested and would lose the low-cost data point. D's one change is a cap of 1 retry on tickets over the long-ticket token threshold. I log this in `disagreements.md` with you as the owner. |
| P4 | Adopt | At n=3, B's 0.02 miss cannot be told apart from noise. |

**Round 3 requirement table** (appended to `spe/spec/spec.md`)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3.1 | Config C exposes the outage status check as its own tool. All other merged tools stay merged. | r02 F4, P1 | C's tool manifest lists `outage_status` on its own. The transcript scan counts calls to it on outage tickets. |
| R3.2 | Config D allows at most 1 retry on long tickets. | r02 F6, default replacing P3 | Code check: no D transcript has more than 1 retry on a long ticket. |
| R3.3 | A and B do not change. They are the controls. | P4 rationale | Config hashes for A and B match r02. |
| R3.4 | Add 10 hard tickets (H01 to H10) that mix billing and outage. Grade them as a separate slice. | P2 | `tickets/hard/` has 10 tickets. Every result row carries `slice: original` or `slice: hard`. |
| R3.5 | Each hard ticket's label is written by one Opus subagent and checked by a second Opus subagent working on its own. A ticket the two disagree on is fixed or dropped before launch. | P2, default | The gate log shows that both labelers agree on every kept ticket. |
| R3.6 | Run 5 trials per cell. A split cell gets extra trials, up to 8. | P4 | The trial count per cell is 5, or between 6 and 8 for a cell flagged as split. |
| R3.7 | The grader reads priority from `label.priority` only. | r02 F5 | A selftest case has a draft reply that says P1 and a label that says P3. It must grade as P3. |
| R3.8 | Trials cannot read graders, answer keys, or predictions. | SPE way | The transcript scan finds no reads of `grade.py`, `keys/`, or `predictions/`. Any trial that read one is voided. |

**Defaults logged in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`** (owner: you)
- D gets a retry cap instead of being dropped (P3).
- Claude authors the hard-ticket labels, and a second Opus agent cross-checks them. A human has not reviewed them.
- The original set is 20 tickets until I confirm the count.

Commit: `SPE r03 specify: adopt P1 P2 P4, replace P3 with D retry cap`

## 2. Predict

The baseline comes from `spe/predictions/r03-draft.yaml` and the round 2 log. A hit means the measured value falls inside the band. The Closer column compares my number with the "same as last round" number.

**Original slice (20 tickets x 5 trials = 100 graded per cell)**

| Metric | Config | Same as last round | Predicted | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | A | 0.86 | 0.86 ± 0.04 | `label.category` exact match | A is unchanged. |
| category accuracy | B | 0.86 | 0.86 ± 0.04 | `label.category` exact match | B is unchanged. Round 2 showed its predicted gain over A was noise. |
| category accuracy | C | 0.80 | 0.80 ± 0.05 | `label.category` exact match | The status check sets priority, not category. Splitting it out should leave category where it is. |
| category accuracy | D | 0.74 | 0.74 ± 0.05 | `label.category` exact match | The retry cap only changes how often D retries. It does not change the first answer. |
| priority accuracy | C | 0.71 | 0.77 ± 0.05 | `label.priority` exact match (F5 fix) | F4 put outage tickets at P3. With the lookup back, C should return close to its r01 level of 0.78. |
| outage lookup call rate on outage tickets | C | 0.00 | 0.90 ± 0.10 | Code scan of transcripts for `outage_status` calls | This tests R3.1 directly. A separate tool is visible to the agent, so the agent calls it. |
| cost per ticket | D | $0.004 | $0.003 ± $0.0007 | Token counts from the API usage field x price table | F6 doubled tokens on long tickets. Capping retries removes most of that excess. |

**Hard slice (10 tickets x 5 trials = 50 graded per cell)**

The baseline for this slice is the same config's round 2 value on the original set. That baseline is what the Closer column compares against.

| Metric | Config | Naive baseline | Predicted | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | A | 0.86 | 0.70 ± 0.10 | `label.category` exact match | A mixed ticket carries 2 category signals, so it is harder to label than a single-topic ticket. |
| category accuracy | B | 0.86 | 0.70 ± 0.10 | `label.category` exact match | B is the same as A, and round 2 showed no real gap between them. |
| category accuracy | C | 0.80 | 0.66 ± 0.10 | `label.category` exact match | C starts 0.06 below A on the original set. I keep that gap. |
| category accuracy | D | 0.74 | 0.58 ± 0.10 | `label.category` exact match | D starts lowest. The hard tickets are also long, so the retry cap hits D here most. |

Each config changes 1 thing: A none, B none, C adds the split outage tool, D adds the retry cap. The hard slice is a change to the task set, not to any config, so I score it as its own slice.

**After approval, before any harness work**
1. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`.
2. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml`. It starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It holds `round: 3`, `date: 2026-10-21`, and `author: Claude, approved by the user in plan mode`. It also holds the configs, every number above with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round`. I leave `r03-draft.yaml` in place as history.
3. Commit: `SPE r03 predict: C priority 0.77, C lookup 0.90, D cost $0.003, hard slice 0.58 to 0.70`

## 3. Evaluate

**Script:** `spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`. One constant at the top holds the round: `const ROUND = 3`. Prompt text, paths, and result names all come from `ROUND`. No round number is typed into a prompt by hand.

**Gates (each must pass before the next step. A failure halts the run and reports.)**
1. **Hard-ticket labels.** Opus labeler 1 writes `spe/evals/keys/r03-hard.yaml`. Opus labeler 2 labels the same tickets without seeing labeler 1's output. The gate passes when they agree on every kept ticket and at least 8 of 10 tickets are kept.
2. **Grader selftest.** The oracle answers must score 1.0. Empty answers must score 0. Wrong answers must score 0. The F5 case (draft reply says P1, label says P3) must grade as P3.
3. **Control regrade of round 2.** The grader regrades the saved r02 outputs. It must reproduce the regraded r02 numbers within 0.005: A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80 on category, and C 0.71 on priority.
4. **Config check.** A and B hashes match r02. C's manifest has `outage_status` on its own. D's config has `max_retries_long: 1`.
5. **Dry run.** Run 1 trial in each of 3 cells: A on T01, C on T17 (the F4 ticket), and D on H01. Check the schema, the grading, the transcript scan, and the cost logging from end to end.

Commit after the gates pass: `SPE r03 evaluate (harness)`

**Workflow arguments**

| Argument | Value |
|---|---|
| `configs` | `["A","B","C","D"]` |
| `slices` | `original` (T01 to T20), `hard` (H01 to H10, minus any dropped at gate 1) |
| `trials_per_cell` | 5 |
| `split_topup_max` | 8 trials per cell |
| `split_rule` | A cell is split when 2 or 3 of its 5 trials disagree on category or priority |
| `trial_schema` | `{ticket_id, config, trial, label: {category, priority}, draft_reply, tool_calls[], retries, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd}` |
| `cost_cap_usd` | 25.00 for trials, 5.00 for analysis agents |
| `analysis_model` | Opus |

**Run steps**
1. Fan out trials. Each trial sees only the ticket text and its config's tools. Before it starts, each trial checks the remaining budget. If the trial would cross the cap, it is skipped and the skip goes into `skips.jsonl`.
2. Validate every output against the schema. A malformed output counts as a failed trial. It is not retried silently.
3. Scan each transcript for reads of `grade.py`, `keys/`, `predictions/`, or `spe/plans/`. A trial that touched any of them is voided and logged.
4. Grade with code only. Category and priority are exact matches on the label fields. The lookup call rate and the retry count come from `tool_calls` and `retries`. Cost comes from the usage fields. No judge is needed this round, because code can check every metric.
5. Add top-up trials to split cells, up to 8 per cell, within the cost cap.
6. An Opus failure-analysis agent reads the failed trials. It groups them into existing F-types (F4, F6) or proposes new ones. It also checks whether F4 and F6 are actually fixed.
7. An Opus completeness critic checks four things: every predicted cell has a measured value, every void and skip is explained, the control regrade matches, and the trial counts match R3.6.
8. Write the results to `spe/evals/r03/results.json` and `spe/evals/r03/summary.md`.

**Unmeasured cost estimate**
- Trials: 30 tickets x 4 configs x 5 = 600 base trials. D costs about $0.003 per trial, so about $0.45 for its 150 trials. I have no measured per-trial cost for A, B, or C. If I guess $0.02 to $0.03 per trial, their 450 trials cost about $9 to $14. Top-ups add up to about $5.
- Analysis agents: about $2 to $4.
- Total estimate: $12 to $24, under the $30 combined cap. This is a guess. The run measures the real cost.

**Halt and report** when any of these happens: a cost cap is reached, a trial reads an answer key, a gate fails, or a decision needs you. One example of that is fewer than 8 hard tickets surviving gate 1.

## 4. Close-out (after the Workflow completion notice)

- Commit: `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
- `spe/prediction-log.md`: add a round 3 section with Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under it, add "Which Why broke". If the naive guess beat my predictions again, I say so plainly.
- `spe/failures.md`: mark F4 and F6 fixed or still open, and cite the evidence. Add any new F-types with name, kind, round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. If a grader bug turns up, I keep the original and the regraded numbers side by side.
- `spe/spec/spec.md`: add a "Proposed for round 4" table. Write `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- Update `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r03 learn: ...` and tag `spe-r03`.

**Stop check.** Round 2 hit 1 of 5 predictions, so the 3-hits-in-a-row stop rule cannot trigger yet. If every config passes everything on the hard slice, round 4 needs harder tasks or stricter graders.

**Commits.** Every commit is local. I never push. Commit messages carry no Claude attribution, as your CLAUDE.md requires.
